summary:
The rework answers every finding that was accepted:
- **M1:** the Stop trigger now spin-polls and matches by prefix. Only T-011 run A keeps an exact match, and its target is followed by a long listing.
- **M2:** R-004 now has n-slow between the target and z-unread, plus a void rule.
- **M3:** the tree/list swap only happens while ShowTreeButton is visible, and T-010 run 2 checks it.
- **M4:** timing is checked against the 120 s limit, with split ids as the fallback.
- **m1:** the poll spins instead of sleeping.
- **m2:** the header now leads with the 'not read yet' clause and logs whether it fits.
- **m4:** one HasFigures gate, plus rule 2.

m3 stays deferred, as decided.

The engine did not append rule 1 a second time. fitness.yaml holds one copy of each SL-110 rule, at lines 1349 and 1365.

What is left is small and comes from the rework itself. All four findings are minor:
- **T-010 run 3 cannot run as written.** It uses TreeMode's Release, which refuses without FSA_HOOK_SELECT (TreeMode.cs:109-110). TreeMode also runs no walk and logs no radio state after Release, so the second-ending checks have nothing to read.
- **The new hook reads of LastResult.Store can keep the stopped store alive.** Run 3's store-released check needs them to follow the existing WeakStore discipline. One cached strong reference makes it fail falsely.
- **Rule 1's text in fitness.yaml is stale.** It still names the attempt-1 header 'Folders marked not read yet…'. The new header 'Not read yet: …' is a third, independent spelling of the word that rule 1 cannot see.
- **Rule 2's regex was not tried against other spellings (CC-007).** Its text claims more than a tripwire does.

findings.claim:
T-010 run 3 is specified as 'stop at m-mid\, choose the tree, then Release to a small completed root', using 'the existing Release step ... with no change'. That will not work as written, for two reasons.

1. TreeMode refuses FSA_HOOK_RELEASE unless FSA_HOOK_SELECT is also set. Run 3 names no SELECT, so it ends in a refusal before Release runs.
2. TreeMode.Drive's fixed order is WaitForEnding, Walk, Recycle, ExpandTimed, Multiply, Select, Release, Gap. Nothing walks or logs view state after Release. Two of the checks run 3 promises at the second ending therefore have no log line to read: 'Folders is checked' and 'no walked row draws not read yet'. Only the second-ending line, with treeChoice if that field is added in WaitForEnding, and the two store-released lines exist.
findings.evidence: TreeMode.cs:109-110 is the refusal. TreeMode.cs:121-137 is the step order. Release (TreeMode.cs:563-585) emits only store-released and second-ending. The design's T-010 run 3 reads: 'At the second ending ShowTreeButton is hidden, Folders is checked, the completed tree shows, and no walked row draws not read yet.'

quote.text: throw new Refusal("FSA_HOOK_RELEASE needs FSA_HOOK_SELECT: the row a person had selected before picking a new folder");

findings.fix: Give run 3 FSA_HOOK_SELECT, naming a stopped-tree row such as p04, which also exercises a selected row in a closed session. Add a post-Release step to TreeMode, under FSA_HOOK_TREE_STOP or a new switch, that logs ShowTreeButton visibility and ShowFoldersButton.IsChecked and walks the second tree one level deep. Alternatively, drop the 'no walked row' clause and check only the second-ending line.

findings.evidence: TreeMode.cs:587-595 (WeakStore, NoInlining, 'no local of the caller keeps the store alive'). TreeMode.cs:563-585: Release asserts Collected(store) when the second scan starts and when it ends. The design's tree-mode additions read 'LastResult.Store' in four places.

quote.text: // Only a weak reference leaves this method, and it is not inlined, so no local of the caller keeps the store

findings.fix: Route every new store read through one NoInlining helper in StoppedTree.cs, for example StoreFacts(window, entries). It resolves LastResult.Store by reflection on each call and returns only values (bools, counts, strings), never the store or a delegate bound to it. State in the design that no hook field or closure may hold the store.

findings.claim:
Rule 1 now has two problems.

1. **Its stored text is stale.** The entry at fitness.yaml:1349-1363 is attempt 1's. It still says the stopped headers' prose is 'Rows marked not read yet…' and 'Folders marked not read yet…'. The design now says the second header is 'Not read yet: folders…', and the design's own copy of the rule's text was updated, but the entry the engine kept was not. A rule's text describing a header that no longer exists is the kind of overclaim Q-251 asked to keep out of rule text.
2. **The new header is a third copy of the word.** 'Not read yet: folders the stop came before. …' is a capitalised literal of its own, not built from TopLevelRowText.NotReadYet. Rule 1 cannot see it, because its patterns need a quote or a parenthesis around the phrase. If the constant is ever reworded, the list title and the tree note follow it, but the header goes on explaining a word that no longer appears. The one-word rule therefore holds for two of the three surfaces only by construction.
findings.evidence: fitness.yaml:1355-1361, the because text naming ''Folders marked not read yet…''. The design's 'Stopped-ending tree choice' component gives the header as $"Not read yet: folders the stop came before. Largest first, by space on disk, of what was read in {root}". The design's rule 1 text gives 'Not read yet: folders…'.

quote.text: ''Folders marked not read yet…'') does not match either pattern.

findings.fix: Build the header's lead from the constant, for example `$"{char.ToUpperInvariant(TopLevelRowText.NotReadYet[0])}{TopLevelRowText.NotReadYet[1..]}: folders the stop came before. …"`. Edit fitness.yaml:1358-1359 so the because names the actual headers, 'Rows marked not read yet…' and 'Not read yet: folders…'.

findings.evidence: fitness.yaml:1366-1376, rule 2's pattern and because text. CC-007 asks that a regex be tried against the repository's syntactic variants. Lesson #486: 'Word text rules as tripwires'.
findings.fix: Add one sentence to the because text: 'A tripwire for the guard as written today, not a closed class; == null, a get-accessor body or an extra condition escape it'. Optionally widen the pattern to `(?:is\s+null|==\s*null)`. The HasFigures gate is what actually closes the class; the rule only flags a regression.
findings.class_of: figure-guard spellings rule 2's regex does not see

dimensions_checked.result:
None new.
- CurrentFolder as the last committed folder: measured (spike 120) and consistent with Scanner.cs:413-415.
- Thread.Sleep granularity: now only the reason for spinning, and the spin's cost was measured.
- NTFS name order: measured on spike 120's fixture. On T-010 and R-004 each void rule catches a wrong order.
- RadioButton grouping: recalled, with a stated fallback (wire ShowFoldersButton) if it fails.

The earlier M1 and M2 are answered. Every Stop target except T-011 run A is a prefix match, so the Stop lands somewhere in a whole subtree: about 20 ms for m-mid, 0.16 s for n-slow, 0.5 s for m-big. R-004 has n-slow between the target and z-unread and a note-based void rule. T-010's void rule needs not-listed rows at both depth 1 and depth 2. Nothing new found.

m2: the new hook reads of LastResult.Store can keep the stopped store alive. Nothing forces them through a weak-reference or values-only helper, and run 3's release check depends on that. The HasFigures gate answers my earlier m4.
None. T-010's third run, the VIEWS switch and the SL-100/SL-063 guards each serve a named seam: StartScan's reset, the view gate, and the ShowTopLevel/ShowOutcome edits (#411). Rule 2 is one regex.

m1: T-010 run 3 uses Release without the SELECT it requires (TreeMode.cs:109-110). TreeMode also has no step after Release that could show 'Folders checked' or 'no walked row draws not read yet' at the second ending. The earlier M3 (the Folders arm) is answered by gating the swap on ShowTreeButton being visible.

No new gap. The earlier m3 (Q-071's wrap around the on-demand build) was deferred by decision and is filed for later; it is not re-filed here. OffersStoppedTree keeps the two known throw shapes out, and a Core Fact pins it.

m4: rule 2's regex was not tried against other spellings (CC-007), and its text does not call it a tripwire (#486).

Checked and fine:
- fitness.yaml holds one copy of each SL-110 rule, at lines 1349 and 1365. The engine did not append rule 1 twice.
- WindowCases' All list already includes R-001 and R-002 (line 150), so R-004 joining All follows the existing practice.
- SL-106 links TopLevelRowText.cs alone, so the new constant compiles there.
- SL-063 and SL-100 reference the App project, which is what their new acceptance commands need.
- No bug project links FolderTreeNode.cs or FolderTreeSession.cs.
None. The change is a read-only view over a store whose scan has returned, plus unelevated cases under %LOCALAPPDATA%\Temp. R-004 opens and closes only its own Explorer window, under Q-275.
